rules.title: NJ security deposit cap (1.5 months' rent) and annual increase limit
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase cannot exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent held as security (including last month's rent) counts toward the cap.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede cobrar un depósito de seguridad mayor a una vez y media el alquiler mensual, y cualquier aumento anual no puede exceder el 10% del depósito actual. El alquiler prepagado retenido como garantía (incluido el último mes) cuenta para el límite.
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted unless the tenant requests in writing that the law apply (effective 30 days after request).
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in by written request).
rules.caveat: Secondary summary guide (DCA Truth in Renting); not a statutory text.

rules.title: NJ security deposit return within 30 days; double damages
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear or money owed. If the landlord fails to return it, the tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld plus costs and attorney's fees.
rules.requirement_es: Dentro de los 30 días posteriores al fin del contrato, el arrendador debe devolver el depósito más intereses, menos deducciones detalladas por daños que excedan el desgaste normal o dinero adeudado. Si no lo hace, el inquilino puede demandar por el doble de lo retenido indebidamente más costas y honorarios.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings excepted unless tenant opts in.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (opt-in available).
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees; $500–$2,000 civil penalty for willful withholding from tenants receiving government assistance.

rules.title: NJ security deposit interest and holding requirements
rules.requirement: Interest or earnings on the security deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited to rent annually. The landlord must hold the deposit in trust in an insured NJ bank account and give the tenant written notice of the bank, amount, account type and interest rate within 30 days of receipt.
rules.requirement_es: Los intereses del depósito pertenecen al inquilino y deben pagarse en efectivo o acreditarse al alquiler cada año. El arrendador debe mantener el depósito en fideicomiso en un banco asegurado de NJ y notificar por escrito al inquilino el banco, el monto, el tipo de cuenta y la tasa de interés dentro de 30 días.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals; owner-occupied two-/three-family dwellings excepted unless tenant opts in; seasonal rentals (≤125 days) excluded from the account section.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-/three-family dwellings; seasonal rentals for the deposit-account section.
rules.penalty: If notice/interest not provided, tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent after written notice and 30 days.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to not renew a lease
rules.requirement: Most residential landlords cannot refuse to renew a written or oral lease unless they have a statutory good cause. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excepted.
rules.requirement_es: La mayoría de los arrendadores residenciales no pueden negarse a renovar un contrato, escrito u oral, sin una causa justificada prevista por ley. Se exceptúan las viviendas de dos o tres familias ocupadas por el dueño, moteles/hoteles y unidades transitorias o de temporada.
rules.quoted_span: regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties statewide, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels, transient or seasonal units.
rules.caveat: Only a passing mention in this part of the guide; the list of good causes appears in the Eviction section (later part). Citation given in source as 2A:18:61.3.

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income protected
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents cannot refuse to rent or treat applicants differently based on their source of lawful income (among other protected characteristics). A landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit history.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y agentes no pueden negarse a alquilar ni dar trato desigual a solicitantes por su fuente de ingresos legal (entre otras características protegidas). Aún pueden negarse por ingresos insuficientes o mal historial crediticio.
rules.quoted_span: nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships except two-family owner-occupied dwellings and rooms in owner/resident-occupied single homes.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).
rules.caveat: Secondary summary; quote is the tail of a sentence listing protected classes.
